sentences.text: Pujatopouli is known from a partially preserved skull and postcranial elements, making it one of the most complete Mesozoic crown group birds.
This bird weighed up to 2.03 kg, which is smaller than the contemporary bird Polarornis.
It possessed a long, narrow, straight beak with a pointed end, distinct from the rounded beaks of early galloanserine birds.
Pujatopouli was officially described by Facundo Irazoqui and colleagues in 2026.
The genus name honors Hernán Pujato, combining his surname with the Greek word for bird.
The species name soberana honors the Argentine military group Patrulla Soberanía.
Pujatopouli likely hunted small invertebrates and fish using foot-propelled diving, similar to modern diving birds.
Pujatopouli is classified as an extinct genus of neoavian birds.
Phylogenetic analyses suggest it belongs to the clade Aequornithes and is a sister taxon to Procellaridae.
Pujatopouli lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian stage) in Antarctica.
It lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
It is debated whether Pujatopouli is a definite member of Neoaves, though it shows affinities with Aequornithes.
